acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Mummies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as God-King, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Four-Cartouche Sarcophagus Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A fully wrapped royal dead figure in towering gold-and-lapis headdress and regalia, framed by a sarcophagus lid divided into four cartouche quarters and a permanent sandstorm halo of family-native, non-affinity burial sand rather than Earth or Wind affinity; the halo stays bounded to the royal silhouette and readable rails.

Signature mechanic: Royal Passage: the sarcophagus lid floats behind the God-King like a banner on four linen-and-gold rails. The Knot cartouche pulls Husks from common-grave alcoves; the Bronze cartouche equips survivors as Tomb Guards; the Script cartouche lets a Sacred Servant record a three-point procession; and the Mask cartouche closes a Pharaoh's Champion formation. The towering headdress points to one cartouche while family-native sand follows the moving rail, never acting independently. Cutting the lit cartouche's linen hinge permanently drops that lid quarter and removes its command. After two quarters fall, the God-King steps out of the remaining frame; its headdress shortens with each lost rail and it cycles only surviving rites around exposed wrapping knots.
battlefieldDuty: Command a royal tomb boss through a floating sarcophagus lid and four cartouche rails that bind, guard, rewind, and form lower Mummies before each broken rail simplifies the arena and final wrapped body.
constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity materials remain dry linen, desiccated flesh, bronze, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, turquoise, sandstone grave goods, burial dust, and ordinary tomb sand with visible age and craft.

Motion and effects stay funerary and mechanical: bandages tighten, knots turn, charms strike linen, glyph ink conducts faint ritual light, dust shakes from folds, and sand moves only when a wrapped foot, mask, weapon, or sarcophagus displaces it.
counterplay: Read the named cartouche and lower-form tell, disrupt the required Mummy or route, then cut the exposed linen hinge while the rail is forward; every dropped lid quarter removes one rite, clears an arena lane, and exposes another royal wrapping knot. Affinity signal: Loose end knots, bronze stitches, interrupted glyphs, mask straps, cartouche seals, sarcophagus hinges, and exposed dried flesh preserve every established weak point.
forbiddenTreatments: Treating family-native sand, dust, sandstone, faint glyph light, or gold alone as an elemental affinity
identityInvariants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ocher, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.
telegraph: One lapis headdress vane aligns with a cartouche, its gold glyph becomes faintly readable, the matching lid rail swings forward, and lower Mummies cross their arms in the selected learned posture.
